AR(3) entries use CatalogOrder DT_example three environment levels; AR(3) analysis requires least four scientifically meaningful ordered levels. common fitting pattern identical entries environment_shapes: constructors differ assumptions parameters: ism() factor parameters specifies independent, equal-variance levels. dsm() estimates positive relative variances; atm() chosen subset levels. csm() estimates common correlation, optional heterogeneous variance ratios variance="heterogeneous". ar1m(), ar2m(), ar3m() use stationary ordered-level correlations. AR(2) AR(3) use partial autocorrelations, AR functions offer homogeneous heterogeneous marginal variances. mam() specifies MA(1) MA(2) correlation zero correlation beyond order. usm() estimates fully unstructured positive-definite covariance, whereas corgm() estimates general correlation matrix leaves marginal scale vsm(). fam() fits reduced factor-analytic covariance plus specific variances; rrcm() fits reduced-rank covariance identity remainder. antem() uses modified-Cholesky antedependence covariance ordered levels. ownm() accepts either known positive-definite matrix K user-supplied covariance function. maternm() uses numeric spatial coordinates estimates range smoothness. toeplitzm() estimates general stationary Toeplitz correlation using partial autocorrelations. sar() car() use named spatial weights matrix. SAR accepts general square weights matrix; CAR requires symmetric, non-negative, zero-diagonal adjacency matrix isolated levels. choice driven scientific design: use ordered structures level order meaningful, spatial structures defensible coordinates adjacency, flexible structures usm() corgm() data support larger number parameters.
code: library(sommer) data(DT_example, package="enhancer") DT <- DT_example  env_levels <- unique(as.character(DT$Env)) DT$EnvOrder <- factor(DT$Env, levels=env_levels, ordered=TRUE) DT$EnvCoordinate <- as.numeric(DT$EnvOrder) n_env <- length(env_levels)  # DT_example has three environments. AR(3) needs at least four ordered # levels, so this demonstration-only partition is used for the AR(3) rows # below. Replace it with a scientific time, distance, or ordered factor. DT$CatalogOrder <- factor(rep(seq_len(4L), length.out=nrow(DT)), ordered=TRUE) n_catalog <- nlevels(DT$CatalogOrder)  # Named first-neighbour adjacency among ordered environments. W_env <- matrix(0, n_env, n_env,                 dimnames=list(env_levels, env_levels)) W_env[cbind(seq_len(n_env - 1L), 2:n_env)] <- 1 W_env[cbind(2:n_env, seq_len(n_env - 1L))] <- 1  # A known positive-definite covariance shape for ownm(). K_env <- 0.40 ^ abs(outer(seq_len(n_env), seq_len(n_env), "-"))  # Every object below has the same observation layout and can be used as # a covariance factor in vsm(shape, ism(Name)). Most use EnvOrder; AR(3) # uses CatalogOrder because EnvOrder has too few levels for that structure. environment_shapes <- list(   identity = ism(DT$EnvOrder),   diagonal = dsm(DT$EnvOrder),   selected_diagonal = atm(DT$EnvOrder, levs=env_levels[1:3]),   compound_symmetry = csm(DT$EnvOrder),   compound_symmetry_heterogeneous = csm(     DT$EnvOrder, variance="heterogeneous", values=rep(1, n_env)   ),   ar1 = ar1m(DT$EnvOrder),   ar1_heterogeneous = ar1m(     DT$EnvOrder, variance="heterogeneous", values=rep(1, n_env)   ),   ar2 = ar2m(DT$EnvOrder),   ar2_heterogeneous = ar2m(     DT$EnvOrder, variance="heterogeneous", values=rep(1, n_env)   ),   ar3 = ar3m(DT$CatalogOrder),   ar3_heterogeneous = ar3m(     DT$CatalogOrder, variance="heterogeneous", values=rep(1, n_catalog)   ),   ma1 = mam(DT$EnvOrder, order=1L),   ma2 = mam(DT$EnvOrder, order=2L),   unstructured = usm(DT$EnvOrder),   general_correlation = corgm(DT$EnvOrder),   factor_analytic = fam(DT$EnvOrder, k=1L),   antedependence = antem(DT$EnvOrder, order=1L),   user_defined = ownm(DT$EnvOrder, K=K_env),   reduced_rank = rrcm(DT$EnvOrder, k=1L),   matern = maternm(DT$EnvCoordinate),   toeplitz = toeplitzm(DT$EnvOrder),   sar = sar(DT$EnvOrder, W=W_env),   car = car(DT$EnvOrder, W=W_env) ) fit_environment_shape <- function(shape){   mmes(     Yield ~ Env,     random = ~ vsm(shape, ism(DT$Name)),     rcov = ~ vsm(ism(units)),     data = DT,     verbose = FALSE   ) }  fit_identity <- fit_environment_shape(environment_shapes$identity) fit_ar1 <- fit_environment_shape(environment_shapes$ar1) fit_matern <- fit_environment_shape(environment_shapes$matern) fit_car <- fit_environment_shape(environment_shapes$car)

title: Generalized linear mixed models with sommer
text: Sommer uses penalized quasi-likelihood (PQL). outer iteration tt, linearizes GLMM current link-scale predictor η(t)\eta^{(t)}. μ(t)=g−1(η(t)),hi(t)=dμidηi,Vi(t)=Var(yi∣u), \mu^{(t)} = g^{-1}(\eta^{(t)}), \qquad h_i^{(t)} = \frac{d\mu_i}{d\eta_i}, \qquad V_i^{(t)} = \operatorname{Var}(y_i \mid u), working response diagonal IRLS precision zi(t)=ηi(t)+yi−μi(t)hi(t)−oi,Dii(t)=(hi(t))2Vi(t). z_i^{(t)} = \eta_i^{(t)} + \frac{y_i - \mu_i^{(t)}}{h_i^{(t)}} - o_i, \qquad D_{ii}^{(t)} = \frac{\left(h_i^{(t)}\right)^2}{V_i^{(t)}}. Sommer calls existing weighted Gaussian Henderson/AI-REML solver z(t)z^{(t)}. updates fixed effects, BLUPs, covariance parameters; new predictor η(t+1)=o+Xβ̂+Zû\eta^{(t+1)} = o + X\hat\beta + Z\hat u. outer loop stops deviance change sufficiently small. approach deliberately reuses ai_mme_sp2() weighted Gaussian inner optimizer. maximize exact marginal GLMM likelihood. PQL practical structured large random-effect models, can biased binary sparse count responses, particularly large random-effect variances. Treat standard errors variance components quasi-likelihood approximations settings.

code: data(DT_h2, package="enhancer") DT <- DT_h2  ## build the environmental index ei <- aggregate(y~Env, data=DT,FUN=mean) colnames(ei)[2] <- "envIndex" ei$envIndex <- ei$envIndex - mean(ei$envIndex,na.rm=TRUE) # center the envIndex to have clean VCs ei <- ei[with(ei, order(envIndex)), ]  ## add the environmental index to the original dataset DT2 <- merge(DT,ei, by="Env")  # numeric by factor variables like envIndex:Name can't be used in the random part like this # they need to come with the vsm() structure DT2 <- DT2[with(DT2, order(Name)), ] mix2 <- mmes(y~ envIndex,               random=~ Name + vsm(ism(envIndex),ism(Name)), data=DT2,              rcov=~vsm(dsm(Name),ism(units)),              nIters = 50, verbose = FALSE ) ## Solver selected: ldlt # summary(mix2)$varcomp  b=mix2$uList$`vsm(ism(envIndex), ism(Name` # adaptability (b) or genotype slopes mu=mix2$uList$`vsm(ism(Name`# general adaptation (mu) or main effect e=sqrt(summary(mix2)$varcomp[-c(1:2),"estimate"]) # error variance for each individual  ## general adaptation (main effect) vs adaptability (response to better environments) plot(mu[,1]~b[,1], ylab="general adaptation", xlab="adaptability") text(y=mu[,1],x=b[,1], labels = rownames(mu), cex=0.5, pos = 1) ## prediction across environments Dt <- mix2$Dtable Dt[1,"average"]=TRUE Dt[2,"include"]=TRUE Dt[3,"include"]=TRUE  mix2 <- postPEV(mix2, mode=2) pp <- predict(mix2,Dtable = Dt, D="Name") preds <- pp$pvals # preds[with(preds, order(-predicted.value)), ] ## performance vs stability (deviation from regression line) plot(preds[,2]~e, ylab="performance", xlab="stability") text(y=preds[,2],x=e, labels = rownames(mu), cex=0.5, pos = 1)

title: Theory: how sommer parameterizes and optimizes covariance structures
text: Rather maximizing marginal likelihood yy directly (needs V=ZGZ′+RV = ZGZ' + R, generally dense huge), Henderson’s equations solve β,u\beta,u jointly using R−1R^{-1} Gi−1G_i^{-1}: C(β̂û)=(X′R−1yZ′R−1y),C=(X′R−1XX′R−1ZZ′R−1XZ′R−1Z+G−1) C\begin{pmatrix}\hat\beta\\ \hat u\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}X'R^{-1}y\\ Z'R^{-1}y\end{pmatrix}, \qquad C = \begin{pmatrix} X'R^{-1}X & X'R^{-1}Z\\ Z'R^{-1}X & Z'R^{-1}Z + G^{-1} \end{pmatrix} G−1=blockdiag(G1−1,…,Gr−1)G^{-1} = \mathrm{blockdiag}(G_1^{-1}, \dots, G_r^{-1}). matters parameterization: every quantity sommer actually needs — CC, log-determinant, REML score/AI-matrix — built inverses (R−1R^{-1}, Gi−1G_i^{-1}) derivatives respect θ\theta, never GiG_i RR except invert per structure per iteration. sommer’s internal name Gi−1G_i^{-1} within structure Lambda (Λ=K−1\Lambda = K^{-1}).

Internally, covm uses CovarianceFactor interface vsm. \(2 \times 2\) effect covariance represented using normalized-Cholesky parameterization. guarantees positive-definite covariance matrix optimization. variance first random effect represented overall scale parameter sigma2. remaining variance ratio covariance represented normalized-Cholesky factor. two random effects may different incidence matrices. text: Every CovarianceFactor descriptor carries native reporting callback. Built-structures use report meaningful quantities level-specific variances dsm(), variances covariances usm(), variance-correlation parameters correlation structures. Structural zeros internal coordinates log standard deviations, normalized Cholesky coefficients, variance ratios returned covariance model provides direct native representation. built-CovarianceFactor families provide native reporters, including identity, diagonal, unstructured, AR(1–3), compound-symmetry, moving-average, general-correlation, factor-analytic, antedependence, reduced-rank, Matern, Toeplitz, SAR, CAR structures. Heterogeneous AR compound-symmetry models report dependence parameter together level-specific variances rather overall variance plus variance ratios. fixed estimated covariance parameters included. arbitrary Kronecker product, product-level variance scale absorbed first covariance-shaping factor. Subsequent factors necessarily reported normalized relative scale product one identifiable overall scale. User-defined ownm() structures can supply native_report callback. none supplied, overall variance naturally transformed parameter values returned. Special variance structures vsr(atr(x,levels),y) can used specify heterogeneous variance "y" covariate specific levels covariate "x", e.g., random=~vsr((Location,c("","B")),ID) fits variance component ID levels B covariate Location. vsr(dsr(x),y) can used specify diagonal covariance structure "y" covariate levels covariate "x", e.g., random=~vsr(dsr(Location),ID)  fits variance component ID levels covariate Location. vsr(usr(x),y) can used specify unstructured covariance structure "y" covariate levels  covariate "x", e.g., random=~vsr(usr(Location),ID)  fits variance covariance components ID levels covariate Location. vsr(overlay(...,rlist=NULL,prefix=NULL)) can used specify overlay design matrices consecutive random effects specified, e.g., random=~vsr(overlay(male,female)) overlays (overlaps) incidence matrices male female random effects obtain single variance component effects. `rlist` argument list element numeric value multiplies incidence matrix overlayed. See overlay details.Can combined vsr(). vsr(leg(x,n),y) can used fit random regression model using numerical variable x marks trayectory random effect y. leg function can combined special functions dsr, usr csr. example random=~vsr(leg(x,1),y) random=~vsr(usr(leg(x,1)),y). vsr(x,Gtc=fcm(v)) can used constrain fixed effects multi-response mixed models. vector specifies fixed effect estimated trait. example fixed=cbind(response., response.j)~vsr(Rowf, Gtc=fcm(c(1,0))) means fixed effect Rowf estimated first response second intercept. gvsr(x,y) can used fit variance covariance parameters two random effects. example, indirect genetic effect models. spl2Da(x.coord, y.coord, .var, .levels)) can used fit 2-dimensional spline (e.g., spatial modeling) using coordinates x.coord y.coord (numeric class) assuming single variance component. 2D spline can fitted specific levels using .var .levels arguments. example random=~spl2Da(x.coord=Row,y.coord=Range,.var=FIELD). spl2Db(x.coord, y.coord, .var, .levels)) can used fit 2-dimensional spline (e.g., spatial modeling) using coordinates x.coord y.coord (numeric class) assuming multiple variance components. 2D spline can fitted specific levels using .var .levels arguments. example random=~spl2Db(x.coord=Row,y.coord=Range,.var=FIELD). text: Fits generalized linear mixed model coded C++ using Armadillo Eigen libraries optimize matrix operations. Special covariance structures can specified vsm() function. Two engines available; henderson formulation direct reml (henderson argument) three solvers ; ldlt, cholmod pcg (solver argument) adjust modeling situation.

Within vsm(...), last constructor supplies incidence   matrix main random effect, preceding constructors define   covariance-shaping factors. number covariance factors limited.   example, random = ~ vsm(dsm(Location), ism(Name)) fits heterogeneous variances across Location random effect   Name, random = ~ vsm(dsm(Environment), ar1m(Row), ar1m(Column),   ism(Name), Gu=Ainv) specifies arbitrary Kronecker product covariance structures   relationship matrix Name. Special variance structures vsm(atm(x,levels),ism(y)) can used specify heterogeneous variance "y" covariate specific  levels covariate "x", e.g., random=~vsm((Location,c("","B")),ism(ID))  fits variance component ID levels B covariate Location. vsm(dsm(x),ism(y)) can used specify diagonal covariance structure "y" covariate  levels covariate "x", e.g., random=~vsm(dsm(Location),ism(ID))  fits variance component ID levels covariate Location. vsm(usm(x),ism(y)) can used specify unstructured covariance structure "y" covariate  levels  covariate "x", e.g., random=~vsm(usm(Location),ism(ID))  fits variance covariance components ID levels covariate Location. vsm(usm(rrm(x,y,z,nPC)),ism(y)) can used specify unstructured covariance structure "y" effect  levels  covariate "x", response variable "z", e.g.,  random=~vsm(rrm(Location,ID,response, nPC=2),ism(ID))  fits reduced-rank  factor analytic covariance ID 2 principal components covariate Location. vsm(ism(overlay(...,rlist=NULL,prefix=NULL))) can used specify overlay design matrices consecutive random  effects specified, e.g., random=~vsm(ism(overlay(male,female))) overlays  (overlaps) incidence matrices male female random effects obtain  single variance component effects. `rlist` argument list  element numeric value multiplies incidence matrix  overlayed. See redmm  details.Can combined vsm(). vsm(leg(x,n),ism(y)) can used fit random regression model using numerical variable x   marks trayectory random effect y. leg function can   combined special functions dsm, usm csm.   example random=~vsm(leg(x,1),ism(y)) random=~vsm(usm(leg(x,1)),ism(y)). spl2Dc(x.coord, y.coord, .var, .levels)) can used fit 2-dimensional spline (e.g., spatial modeling) using   coordinates x.coord y.coord (numeric class) assuming   multiple variance components. 2D spline can fitted specific   levels using .var .levels arguments. example   random=~spl2Dc(x.coord=Row,y.coord=Range,.var=FIELD).
